John Messinger

Republican candidate for Court of Criminal Appeals, Place 9, Texas

Assistant State Prosecuting Attorney, Office of the State Prosecuting Attorney (Texas)

John Messinger is a Republican appellate prosecutor who has worked in the Texas Office of the State Prosecuting Attorney since 2011, representing the State before the Court of Criminal Appeals. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Court of Criminal Appeals Place 9 over Jennifer Balido. He faces Democrat Holly Taylor in the November 3, 2026 general election for the open seat now held by Judge David Newell, who is not running again.

Where Messinger stands

Court efficiency / timely rulings
Names efficiency as his top administrative priority for the court. He has spoken about how long it takes the Court of Criminal Appeals to issue rulings.
Judicial approach
Says appellate judges should decide cases from the written record and the law, not from sympathy for a party, and argues this lets cases be judged without regard to factors such as race or ethnicity.
Endorsements
Endorsed by Texas Right to Life, Texas Alliance for Life, and the Combined Law Enforcement Associations of Texas (CLEAT), along with some statewide and local conservative groups.

Background

  • Assistant State Prosecuting Attorney, Office of the State Prosecuting Attorney, 2011–present
  • Earlier: McLennan County District Attorney's Office (direct appeals, protective orders, civil matters)
  • Chair, State Bar of Texas Pattern Jury Charges – Criminal Committee
  • Has filed more than 100 petitions for discretionary review with the Court of Criminal Appeals
  • Republican nominee, Third Court of Appeals Place 2, 2024 (lost the general election)
  • Won the 2026 Republican primary for Court of Criminal Appeals Place 9 with about 69% of the vote
  • J.D., Baylor Law School
  • Has never held judicial office
